I see - the web_fetch result is fed as `_last_tool_result`. Let me work with that directly. Let me fetch individual papers one at a time with smaller queries to get complete data.

```python
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

# Fetch the complete XML and parse it
url = 'https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:%22multimodal+RAG%22&start=0&max_results=5&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending'
result = web_fetch(url, max_chars=12000)

# Parse the XML content
xml_content = result['content']
root = ET.fromstring(xml_content)
ns = {'atom': 'http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom'}

entries = root.findall('atom:entry', ns)
print(f"Found {len(entries)} entries")

for i, entry in enumerate(entries):
    title = entry.find('atom:title', ns).text.strip().replace('\n', ' ')
    paper_id = entry.find('atom:id', ns).text.split('/abs/')[-1]
    summary = entry.find('atom:summary', ns).text.strip().replace('\n', ' ')
    published = entry.find('atom:published', ns).text
    authors = [a.find('atom:name', ns).text for a in entry.findall('atom:author', ns)]
    print(f"\n[{i+1}] {title}")
    print(f"    ID: {paper_id}")
    print(f"    Date: {published[:10]}")
    print(f"    Authors: {', '.join(authors[:3])}...")
    print(f"    Summary: {summary[:200]}...")
```
